steps.say: A pronoun stands in for a noun. It must be clear who or what it means.
A possessive pronoun can stand alone. Mine, yours, hers, ours and theirs are examples.
An abstract noun names an idea or feeling. You cannot touch it.
Use fewer for things you can count and less for things you cannot count.

check.prompt: Which word can stand alone as a possessive pronoun?

options.why: Our needs a noun after it.
Us is not a possessive pronoun.

hints: A possessive pronoun can end a sentence.
check.explanation: Ours can stand alone: That seat is ours.

options.text: There are less pencils on the desk.
options.why: Pencils can be counted, so use fewer.

options.text: There is fewer water in the jug.
options.why: Water is not counted, so use less.

options.text: We have fewer chairs than last year.

options.why: Juice is not counted, so use less.

hints: Can you count the thing one by one?
check.explanation: Chairs are countable, so fewer is correct.
